findings.title: Every history-aware edit runs THREE full-graph O(total-config-size) passes (deep-clone + canonicalize-stringify + uncached panel-context stringify), not one
findings.description: The Phase-0 map (region-maps.json:1930 / leads/frontend.json:122) flagged this as a single 'JSON.stringify node.data.config per edit'. A full code-trace shows it is materially worse: each call to the history-aware setNodes/setEdges/setPreamble performs THREE independent traversals of the ENTIRE graph, not one, and one of them re-serializes preview result columns. Per single edit (e.g. one rating-table cell blur → updateTable → commitTables → handleConfigUpdate → onUpdateNode → setNodes): (1) pushSnapshotInternal()→captureGraphSnapshot()→cloneGraphValue() DEEP-CLONES every node and every edge — a full recursive walk and reallocation of every config object in the graph, including the N-1 nodes that did not change; (2) computePersistedFingerprint()→serializeSnapshot()→canonicalize() recursively key-sorts and rebuilds every node's entire data tree into fresh objects/arrays and then JSON.stringify()s the whole graph; (3) computePanelContextFingerprint()→panelContextNodeDataHash() JSON.stringify()s config + _columns + _availableColumns + _schemaWarnings for EVERY node with no memo cache. Only the 4th pass (computeStructuralFingerprint→shallowNodeDataHash) is WeakMap-cached so unchanged nodes are cheap there. The other three are not.
findings.evidence: setNodes body (442-466) calls, in one set(): pushSnapshotInternal() (414-421, clones whole graph via captureGraphSnapshot 123-131 → cloneGraphValue 133-154), computePersistedFingerprint (350-352 → serializeSnapshot graphSnapshot.ts:106-118 → canonicalize 78-88 rebuilds every nested object + JSON.stringify of all nodes/edges), computePanelContextPatch (393-405 → computePanelContextFingerprint 330-348 → panelContextNodeDataHash 321-328 with `parts.push(JSON.stringify(value))` per key per node, no WeakMap), and computeStructuralFingerprint (295-307). Three of these four are O(sum of all node config sizes); cloneGraphValue and canonicalize additionally allocate a full copy of the graph each. shallowNodeDataHash (shallowNodeHash.ts:88-99) is the only one with a per-data WeakMap.
findings.when_it_bites: A large ratebook RATING_STEP node holds config.tables as a cartesian product of factor levels (normaliseRatingTables/buildCartesianEntries, ratingTableUtils.ts:106-142): 3 factors × ~50 levels each ≈ 125k entry objects in one config. The editor commits the ENTIRE tables array on every single cell blur (RatingStepEditor.tsx:298-303 commitTables→updateTable; ControlledNumberCell commits onBlur). So each keystroke-commit deep-clones + canonicalizes + stringifies that ~MB-scale config two-to-three times plus once more for every other node in the graph. At ~10k+ total entries this is tens of ms of main-thread work per cell edit — perceptible input lag and GC churn while tabbing through a rating grid. Negligible for small graphs (<~1k total config entries).
findings.recommended_fix: Decouple the three concerns and stop re-walking unchanged nodes. (a) Replace cloneGraphValue with structuredClone, or — since history only needs an immutable reference and config objects are already replaced immutably by handleConfigUpdate (NodePanel.tsx:609-617) — store shallow snapshots (spread nodes/edges) rather than deep clones; the deep clone defends against React-Flow in-place mutation of position only, which a shallow {...n} already isolates. (b) Add a WeakMap<data,string> memo to panelContextNodeDataHash exactly as shallowNodeHash.ts already does, so only the edited node re-stringifies. (c) Consider deriving persistedFingerprint incrementally from the per-node structural hashes (which are already WeakMap-cached) instead of a fresh whole-graph canonicalize+stringify, or memoize serializeSnapshot per node. Each is independently safe and test-covered by the existing dirty/structuralVersion suites.

findings.title: Panel-context fingerprint re-JSON.stringifies every node's preview-result columns (_columns/_availableColumns) on every edit, with no memo cache
findings.description: computePanelContextFingerprint runs on every history-aware edit AND on every structural setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw change (via computePanelContextPatch). Its per-node hash, panelContextNodeDataHash, includes the result-derived keys _columns, _availableColumns and _schemaWarnings in addition to config, and JSON.stringify()s each of them for EVERY node every time — there is no WeakMap cache (contrast shallowNodeDataHash which caches by data identity). So the cost is O(sum over all nodes of (config size + column-list size)). _columns/_availableColumns are full upstream/preview column schemas that can be large on wide ratebooks, and they change whenever a preview completes — coupling preview-completion churn into the per-edit panel-context hash.
findings.evidence: PANEL_CONTEXT_NODE_DATA_KEYS (309-319) lists `config`, `_columns`, `_availableColumns`, `_schemaWarnings`. panelContextNodeDataHash (321-328): `for (const key of ...) parts.push(value === undefined ? '' : JSON.stringify(value) ?? String(value))` — no caching. computePanelContextFingerprint (330-348) maps this over ALL nodes and sorts. Invoked from setNodes/setEdges (451,479), setNodesRaw/setEdgesRaw (549,576), undo/redo (661-664,692-695). Compare shallowNodeHash.ts:23-25,88-99 which memoizes via nodeDataHashCache WeakMap.
findings.when_it_bites: Graphs with many nodes carrying wide column schemas (e.g. a ratebook pipeline where each node's _availableColumns lists hundreds of columns). Every config keystroke-commit re-stringifies all of those column arrays for every node. Also fires redundantly every time any node's preview lands and writes _columns, bumping panelContextVersion and re-running usePanelGraphContext's full nodes.map(toSimpleNode) rebuild (usePanelGraphContext.ts:39-65). At ~50 nodes × ~200 columns this is a few ms of pure stringify per edit and per preview; trivial at small column counts.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a `const panelContextHashCache = new WeakMap<Record<string,unknown>, string>()` and short-circuit panelContextNodeDataHash on cache hit (same pattern as shallowNodeHash.ts). Because handleConfigUpdate and the preview writer both replace node.data immutably, the WeakMap keys are stable per logical version, so only nodes whose data object actually changed re-stringify. Optionally split column-schema identity out via columnFingerprint (utils/columnFingerprint.ts) instead of JSON.stringify of the full column arrays.

findings.title: setNodesRaw position-only fast path still recomputes the full-graph persisted fingerprint on every drag frame
findings.description: setNodesRaw is the path React Flow uses for mid-drag position events (the store docstring at lines 28-33 notes onNodesChange replays many position events per frame). It correctly skips history push and skips the structural fingerprint when only positions changed (hasOnlyNodePositionChanges → computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes, which is cheap). HOWEVER, that branch is reached only AFTER the UI-only check; the genuinely position-only branch at 530-534 returns early and is fine — but note the dirty derivation there (computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes 377-391) walks all nodes comparing saved positions each frame (O(N) per frame). This is bounded and far cheaper than the config-stringify path, so it is low impact; flagging only to confirm the drag path was checked and is NOT running the expensive serializeSnapshot/clone path. The expensive paths (computePersistedFingerprint at 536-540) are only hit when the change is NOT position-only or UI-only, i.e. on actual structural/config edits, which is correct.
findings.evidence: setNodesRaw (523-567): hasOnlyNodeUiFieldChanges→return {nodes} (527-529, cheapest); hasOnlyNodePositionChanges→return {nodes, dirty: computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes(state,nodes)} (530-534) where computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes (377-391)→hasSameSavedNodePositions (365-375) loops all nodes; only the fall-through (536+) calls computePersistedFingerprint/computeStructuralFingerprint. So drag frames avoid the clone+stringify path. Confirmed correct design.
findings.when_it_bites: Only at very large node counts (thousands) during a continuous drag would the per-frame O(N) position comparison in computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes/hasSameSavedNodePositions become noticeable. For typical graphs it is negligible. Included as a verified non-issue / lower bound rather than a defect.
findings.recommended_fix: No change required for realistic sizes. If thousands-of-nodes drags ever matter, short-circuit computeDirtyForPositionOnlyNodes when persistedFingerprint already differs from saved (it returns true immediately in that case at line 387, so only the all-clean case pays the O(N) walk). Leave as-is otherwise.

findings.title: usePanelGraphContext rebuilds the entire SimpleNode/SimpleEdge graph + nodeById Map on every config edit and every preview completion
findings.description: usePanelGraphContext memoizes on panelContextVersion, which (by design, finding above) bumps on every config edit and every preview-column write. On each bump it rebuilds the full snapshot: nodes.map(toSimpleNode) (spreading every node's data), edges.map(toSimpleEdge), and a fresh `new Map(allNodes.map(...))`. This is O(N nodes + E edges) of allocation per edit, feeding NodePanel's allNodes/nodeMap. It is correct and intentionally coarse (keyed away from position churn), but combined with the per-edit fingerprint passes it adds another full-graph allocation to each keystroke-commit. Lower impact than the stringify passes because it is plain object spreads (no JSON), but it does discard and rebuild the whole derived graph view even when only one node's config changed.
findings.evidence: buildSnapshotForVersion (51-55) pulls nodes/edges from getState and calls buildSnapshot (39-49): `nodes.map(toSimpleNode)` (toSimpleNode 14-27 spreads node.data), `edges.map(toSimpleEdge)`, `new Map(allNodes.map(node => [node.id, node]))`. useMemo dep is [panelContextVersion] only (59-65). panelContextVersion increments on every config-bearing edit (useGraphStore computePanelContextPatch 393-405) and whenever _columns/_availableColumns change.
findings.when_it_bites: Large graphs (hundreds of nodes/edges) where the user is actively editing config in a panel: each keystroke-commit triggers a full rebuild of allNodes + nodeById feeding the open panel. At ~50 nodes it is sub-millisecond; at several hundred nodes with the per-edit fingerprint work it compounds into the same input-lag window. Not a concern for small graphs.
findings.recommended_fix: If profiling shows this matters at scale, derive SimpleNode entries lazily/per-id (the only hot consumer is nodeMap[edge.source] lookups and the selected node), or memoize toSimpleNode per node.data via a WeakMap so unchanged nodes keep identity and the Map can be incrementally updated. Acceptable as-is for current graph sizes; primary fix is the fingerprint memoization above which reduces how often panelContextVersion churns.

findings.title: Ratebook rates table renders all levels of the selected factor without virtualization
findings.description: RatebookRatesTab renders one <tr> per row in selectedRows for the chosen factor inside a max-h-80 scroll container, with no windowing. For a high-cardinality factor (e.g. a postcode/vehicle factor with thousands of levels) this mounts thousands of DOM rows even though only ~15 are visible. Unlike DataPreview (which windows both rows via slice(startIdx,endIdx) and columns), this table has no virtualization. It is display-only and rebuilt only when a solve result lands (useMemo on factorTables), not per-edit, so it does not sit on the keystroke hot path — hence low impact — but it can still jank when the user opens the Rates tab on a many-level factor.
findings.evidence: selectedRows.map (111-123) renders every row; container is `overflow-auto max-h-80` (98). selectedRows is the full level list for one factor (44). levelCount across all factors is summed at 45. Contrast DataPreview.tsx:346 `data.preview.slice(startIdx, endIdx).map(...)` and :304 column windowing — the established virtualization pattern this tab does not use.
findings.when_it_bites: Opening the Ratebook Rates tab for a factor with thousands of levels (large geographic/vehicle rating tables). Rendering N thousand rows at once is a one-time layout/paint cost of tens to hundreds of ms and elevated memory; scrolling thereafter is fine because of max-h-80. Bounded factors (tens to low-hundreds of levels) are unaffected.
findings.recommended_fix: Apply the same scroll-window pattern DataPreview already uses (a startIdx/endIdx slice driven by scrollTop, rendering a top/bottom spacer), or only render the first K rows with a 'show more'. Reuse DataPreview's windowing approach for consistency. Low priority — it is off the per-edit path and only affects an explicitly opened display tab.
